subject: Customer segmentation & SLO alignment — follow-up and proposed controls
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Meyers <jacob.meyers@finova.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Customer segmentation & SLO alignment — follow-up and proposed controls

Hi Jacob — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we discussed. I wanted to capture the scope so everyone has a single reference.

Key pain points you shared:
- Large variance in per-customer traffic (10x between smallest and largest) creating noisy autoscaling and cost unpredictability.
- Need predictable P99/P95 latency for premium customers during bursts.
- Regulatory requirement to segregate data handling for a subset of customers and to provide audit logs for rate enforcement decisions.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Ingest + routing in-house (K8s), per-customer metadata in Postgres, authentication via SSO.
- Using mixed model fleet (open models + vendor-hosted models) for different features.

Success criteria (Finova cares about):
- Tiered SLOs: p95 <= 150ms for premium, p95 <= 400ms for standard.
- Per-customer rate caps and burst windows (e.g., base qps + 5x burst for 1 minute).
- Audit trail of routing decisions and quota changes retained for at least 12 months.

Proposed controls we’ll draft for you (attached: two artifacts):
- A proposed QoS configuration (YAML) with per-customer caps, burst policy, and default fallbacks. (proposed-qos-config.yaml)
- A short MAU gap worksheet that maps current consumption to suggested tiers (mau-gap-analysis.xlsx).

Assumptions / open questions we flagged during the call:
- Need confirmation on whether burst allowances should be billed as overage or absorbed by tiered capacity.
- Do you want hard throttles or token-bucket graceful degradation for standard customers?
- Which customer IDs require separate audit retention and which can live under the shared retention policy?

Next steps (action items):
1) We will send a detailed QoS playbook and a configuration proposal by EOD Monday (Hannah + Karthik).
2) Finova to confirm burst billing preference and list of customers needing segregated audit retention by next Wednesday.
3) Schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive (routing + KV cache behavior) once you review the draft.

Attachments: proposed-qos-config.yaml (YAML snippet), mau-gap-analysis.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — will follow up with the config doc.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 18:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Customer segmentation & SLO alignment — follow-up and proposed controls

Thanks Hannah — this is very helpful and close to what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Burst behavior: we prefer graceful degradation (token-bucket style) for standard customers to avoid hard failures; premium customers should have reserved capacity.
- Billing: ideally overages should be visible itemized in the invoice; we can tolerate short bursts without immediate billing but want monthly reconciliations.
- Audit retention: please treat customers with regulated profiles (I’ll send the list) as needing 24-month logs. Others can be 12 months.

Action: I’ll share a CSV with the regulated customer IDs by COB Tuesday. Also looping in our platform alias for scheduling purposes.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — the proposed QoS YAML will help our infra team validate quickly.

—Jacob

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 07:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer segmentation & SLO alignment — follow-up and proposed controls

Jacob — quick technical note: agree on token-bucket for standard tiers. For premium customers we recommend a two-tier enforcement: soft-reservation (guaranteed sockets) + hard cap for total sustained qps. That lets us keep p95 tight while still allowing short bursts.

Regarding auditing, Redwood can include a per-customer routing log (JSON lines) that records: timestamp, chosen model variant, routing decision reason, and quota tokens consumed. We can export to your S3 or to our audit endpoint.

I’ll include concrete p95/p99 targets in the config doc. Hannah — adding a line item for export destinations.

—Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Deliverables (we will share by EOD Monday):
- QoS playbook (YAML + narrative) with per-segment defaults, burst policy, and billing flags.
- MAU tier mapping spreadsheet with suggested pricing bands and migration notes.
- Export options for audit logs (S3 + direct webhook) and retention settings.

Scheduling: I proposed two slots on your calendar for the tech deep-dive: Tuesday 6/15 10:00–10:45 PT or Wednesday 6/16 14:00–14:45 PT. Please pick one or send alternative times.

If you confirm the regulated customers CSV by Tuesday COB, we’ll bake the 24-month retention flag into the config.

Thanks — sending the artifacts shortly.
